stem.text: The Labrador retriever is a breed of dog that, as an adult, shows continuous variation in body mass.
Explain what is meant by continuous variation.

points.text: range of values / range of phenotypes / intermediates ; A do not fall into distinct groups

explanation.text: A definition describes the pattern of the observations: values can lie between other values. It does not require an explanation of why those intermediate phenotypes arise.

reasoningChain: Describe a range with intermediate phenotypes.
Avoid substituting a cause for the definition.

explanation.text: Many loci can make small additive contributions to mass. Environmental differences can shift the phenotype of individuals with similar genotypes, producing many overlapping combinations rather than a few separate groups.

reasoningChain: Connect the combined effects of many genes to the range of masses.

Approximately 25% of Labrador retrievers have at least one mutant POMC allele.

explanation.text: A standard-deviation bar describes variation among individual dogs, rather than the precision of the estimated mean. Overlapping SD bars therefore do not, by themselves, establish the result of a statistical significance test.

reasoningChain: Compare means for named genotypes using kilograms.

stem.text: Labrador retrievers with mutant POMC alleles have changes in behaviour that affect body mass.
Suggest a change in behaviour in Labrador retrievers with mutant POMC alleles that would affect body mass.

points.text: eat more / do less exercise / AW ;

explanation.text: Body mass depends on the balance between energy intake and expenditure. A behavioural change can alter this balance without directly changing the rate of a metabolic enzyme reaction.

reasoningChain: Choose a behaviour that changes intake or expenditure.
Check that the direction of change is consistent with increased body mass.

blocks.heading: Comprehensive responses
bullets: Most responses defined continuous variation as a range of phenotypes without distinct categories.

blocks.heading: Limited responses
bullets: Some responses described causes rather than defining the term.

blocks.heading: Comprehensive responses
bullets: Some responses included polygenic inheritance, environmental factors such as diet and exercise, and their interactions.

blocks.heading: Limited responses
bullets: Some responses treated genetic and environmental factors separately or did not indicate the extent of environmental influence.

blocks.heading: Comprehensive responses
bullets: Most responses correctly identified that the mutant allele increases body mass and supported this using data.
Some responses included accurate figures and recognised overlapping error bars.

blocks.heading: Limited responses
bullets: Some responses omitted units, used imprecise language or did not specify genotype.

blocks.heading: Comprehensive responses
